# Pattern library

<!-- Generated by `node bin/northstar.mjs patterns --markdown`. Do not edit by hand: a test fails if this file drifts from patterns.mjs. -->

Seventy-six canonical patterns (`P01`–`P76`) and thirteen Northstar extensions (`X01`–`X13`). **24** of the 76 canonical patterns and **7** of the extensions are machine-checked from source; the other **58** need a person or a browser, and are listed here so nobody claims coverage they do not have.

Each pattern names the skill that owns the judgement and, where it exists, the engine check that can prove a violation.

## Numbering

- `P01`–`P76` are the 76 patterns of the pattern write-ups, **numbered as they were supplied**. `engine/patterns.ts` uses the same numbers without the padding: `P05` here is `P5` there. The padding exists because severities are also called `P0`–`P3`, and an unpadded `P1` would be ambiguous in a report.
- `X01`+ are Northstar extensions: checks the engine can make that are not among the 76 (alt text, link destinations, target size, form labels, overflow, contrast of non-text UI, …).
- Reports written before the numbering was unified (v1.0.x) used a different index; the last table maps each old id to its current one.
- Ids are stable: findings quote them, so a rule can change without renumbering a report someone is already reading.

Run `node bin/northstar.mjs patterns` for the same list as machine-readable text.

## Checked patterns

| Pattern | Name | Check | The standard it is held to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P05 | Disabled Buttons | `disabled-without-reason`, `disabled-contrast` | A blocked control says what is blocking it, in the place the user is looking. |
| P06 | Hover Trap | `hover-only-action` | Nothing needed to finish the task exists only on hover. |
| P09 | Animation Timing | `no-reduced-motion`, `animate-height-auto`, `transition-all` | Motion is short, purposeful, and absent when the user asked for it to be absent. |
| P11 | Destructive Actions | `native-confirm` | Destruction is named, confirmed in place, and reversible for a few seconds. |
| P21 | Easing Curves | `linear-easing` | One easing family for entrances, one for exits, no bounce on anything the user is reading. |
| P23 | Error States | `native-alert`, `swallowed-error` | An error says what failed, whether it is recoverable, and what to do next. |
| P24 | Form Field States | `placeholder-contrast` | Default, hover, focus, filled, invalid, disabled and read-only are each visibly distinct. |
| P28 | Loading States System | `bare-loading` | Loading is announced, shaped, and finished — never an indefinite spinner with no name. |
| P29 | Navigation Patterns | `nav-missing-current` | The current location is marked, in the nav and in the document title. |
| P44 | Z-Index Mastery | `zindex-arms-race` | Layers come from a short documented scale and a stacking context per surface. |
| P46 | Focus States | `focus-ring-removed`, `no-focus-style`, `tabindex-positive` | Focus is always visible, at 3:1 against what is behind it, and follows the reading order. |
| P50 | Form Validation Timing | `native-alert` | Errors appear when the field is left, not on the first keystroke, and never as a modal. |
| P52 | Optimistic UI | `swallowed-error` | An optimistic update has a rollback and a message for the case where the server refuses. |
| P54 | Skeleton Loading | `bare-loading` | A skeleton has the shape of the content it becomes, so the layout does not jump. |
| P56 | File Upload UX | `disabled-without-reason` | Uploads show the chosen file, its size, progress and a way to remove it before it is sent. |
| P57 | Password Field UX | `unlabelled-input`, `password-autocomplete` | A password field states its rules before submission, offers a reveal toggle, and never blocks paste. |
| P60 | OTP Input | `otp-autocomplete` | A code entry is one field that advances, pastes cleanly, and reports a wrong code without clearing it. |
| P61 | Pagination | `pagination-not-in-url` | The page you are on survives a refresh, a share and the back button. |
| P62 | Accordion Disclosure | `animate-height-auto`, `accordion-without-expanded` | A disclosure announces its state and animates something the browser can actually animate. |
| P63 | Data Table | `table-semantics`, `numeric-cells` | Columns are scoped, numbers line up, and the header stays visible while scrolling. |
| P69 | Design Tokens | `raw-colour-in-class` | One token layer feeds every surface, and `DESIGN.md` records what it contains. |
| P70 | Color Accessibility | `text-contrast`, `disabled-contrast` | Text clears 4.5:1 and large text 3:1 against the colour actually behind it. |
| P72 | Border Radius | `radius-off-scale` | Radii come from one scale, and an inner corner is the outer radius minus the padding. |
| P73 | Dark Mode | `text-contrast` | Dark mode is a token set, not an inverted filter: surfaces stay layered and accents stay legible. |
| X01 | Images, icons and alt text | `image-without-alt`, `image-without-dimensions` | Every image declares its role: described, or explicitly decorative. |
| X02 | Links and destinations | `placeholder-link`, `target-blank-noopener` | A link goes somewhere real; an unconfigured destination is not rendered as `#`. |
| X03 | Touch targets and target size | `small-target` | Every interactive target reaches 24×24 CSS px, and a gesture is never the only route to an action. |
| X05 | Form labels and field anatomy | `unlabelled-input`, `accidental-submit`, `input-type-generic` | Every field has a persistent label, a hint where needed, and an error slot that does not shift the layout. |
| X09 | Overflow and long content | `fixed-width-container` | Long words, long emails and translated strings wrap without breaking the layout, and no container is wider than the viewport. |
| X10 | Contrast of non-text UI | `text-contrast` | Borders, icons and focus rings used to convey state reach 3:1 against their neighbour. |
| X13 | Interactive elements are real controls | `click-on-non-interactive` | Anything that can be clicked is a button, link or input: reachable by Tab, operable with Enter or Space, and announced for what it is. |

## Patterns that need a person

No automated check can settle these from source. A clean `audit` says nothing about them.

| Pattern | Name | Owner | The standard it is held to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P01 | CSS Has Selector | design-system | New CSS is used where it removes JavaScript, with a stated fallback for the browsers the product supports. |
| P02 | De-AI Landing Hero | visual-character | Name the outcome in the headline and the audience in the subtitle. |
| P03 | Reverse-Engineered Linear | design-system | Build depth from three stacked background values plus a hairline border (rgba white at 8%), and change the surface value on hover. |
| P04 | Bulk Actions | feedback-and-affordance | A bulk action names how many items it will affect before it runs. |
| P07 | Date Pickers | form-ux | A date field accepts typing, names its format, and never demands a calendar for a year the user already knows. |
| P08 | Charts That Lie | visual-character | A chart has a title, units, a zero baseline where it means something, and a text alternative. |
| P10 | Context Menu | feedback-and-affordance | A context menu has a keyboard equivalent; right-click is never the only route to an action. |
| P12 | Live Cursors | visual-character | Presence is decoration; it never moves the content the user is reading. |
| P13 | Design System Kit | design-system | Store every value as a named token so color, type, and spacing stay consistent across the app. |
| P14 | Inline Editing | feedback-and-affordance | Editable content looks editable, saves on blur or on Enter, and says whether it saved. |
| P15 | Autosave | state-completeness | A saved-nothing-lost state is visible, and settings changes say whether they applied. |
| P16 | Settings System | state-completeness | Match a setting's apply model to its stakes: instant for low-risk toggles, explicit save for identity. |
| P17 | Behind the Button | state-completeness | The control that started the work shows it is working and cannot be pressed twice; the server re-checks everything the client already checked. |
| P18 | Doherty Threshold | feedback-and-affordance | Every interaction acknowledges itself inside 400ms, even when the work takes longer. |
| P19 | Drag and Drop | feedback-and-affordance | Every drag has a keyboard path, a drop indicator, and an undo. |
| P20 | Dropdown Design | form-ux | A custom select keeps the native keyboard model, including type-ahead and Escape. |
| P22 | Empty States | state-completeness | An empty state explains why it is empty and offers the one action that fills it. |
| P25 | Golden Ratio | design-system | Multiply one base unit by 1.618 to derive both spacing and type scales, so everything shares a rhythm. |
| P26 | Grid System | design-system | Spacing comes from one scale, and density is chosen for the task rather than inherited by accident. |
| P27 | Input Masking | form-ux | Formatting is applied while typing only where it helps, and never silently rewrites a value the user pasted. |
| P30 | Notification System | feedback-and-affordance | Map each notification's severity to the surface that matches it — toast, banner, modal, or badge. |
| P31 | Peak-End Rule | feedback-and-affordance | The last thing a flow says is the thing the user remembers; end on confirmation, not on a spinner. |
| P32 | Proximity Rule | information-hierarchy | Keep spacing within a group tighter than the spacing between groups. |
| P33 | Range Sliders | form-ux | A slider shows its value, its bounds and its step, and accepts keyboard increments. |
| P34 | Search Experience System | state-completeness | Search distinguishes "nothing matched" from "not searched yet", and keeps the query in the URL. |
| P35 | Serial Position | information-hierarchy | The first and last items in a list get the attention; the middle is where items go to be missed. |
| P36 | Shadow Elevation | design-system | Elevation is a small ordered set, and shadow direction agrees with light direction everywhere. |
| P37 | Star Rating | feedback-and-affordance | A rating is a set of radio buttons with a label per value, not five clickable spans. |
| P38 | Stepper Wizard | information-hierarchy | A multi-step flow shows where you are, what is next, and whether you can go back without losing input. |
| P39 | Tabs System | information-hierarchy | Tabs use the tab role pattern, keep their selection in the URL, and do not nest scroll areas. |
| P40 | Toast Notifications | feedback-and-affordance | A toast reports a completed action, does not steal focus, and can be dismissed. |
| P41 | Toggle Anatomy | feedback-and-affordance | A switch changes a setting immediately, announces the new state, and can be undone. |
| P42 | Tooltip Design | feedback-and-affordance | A tooltip adds a hint, never the only copy of the label, and opens on focus as well as hover. |
| P43 | Visual Hierarchy | information-hierarchy | Reserve one accent color for the one action you want users to take. |
| P45 | Zeigarnik Effect | information-hierarchy | Unfinished work is visible and resumable; completed work leaves the working set. |
| P47 | Swipe Actions | feedback-and-affordance | pair each swipe action with an undo window, and keep left/right semantics consistent app-wide. |
| P48 | Undo UX | feedback-and-affordance | Execute the action immediately, then offer a time-limited undo with a visible countdown. |
| P49 | Bottom Sheets | responsive-design | A sheet is dismissible by drag, by Escape and by a visible button, and does not cover its own submit. |
| P51 | Microcopy | visual-character | Labels name the thing; buttons name the action; errors name the fix. |
| P53 | Gradient Design | visual-character | A gradient is a decision about light, not a default background. |
| P55 | Color Picker UX | form-ux | Colour is chosen with a value you can type, and the choice is confirmed beside the sample. |
| P58 | Command Palette | feedback-and-affordance | A palette is reachable from the keyboard, lists the actions the page owns, and closes on Escape. |
| P59 | Filter Chips | feedback-and-affordance | Applied filters are visible, individually removable, and reflected in the result count. |
| P64 | Card Hover Anatomy | visual-character | A card hover lifts or shifts without moving the hit area, and the card has one clear action. |
| P65 | Modal Hierarchy | information-hierarchy | One modal at a time, focus trapped and returned, and a title that says what it is for. |
| P66 | Icon Design Rules | visual-character | Icons share a stroke, a size and an optical weight, and none of them stands alone without a label. |
| P67 | Landing Page Skeleton | visual-character | The hero says what the product does for whom, in the user’s words, with one action. |
| P68 | Scroll-Driven Animations | design-system | Scroll reveals are one-way, cheap, and off under reduced motion. |
| P71 | Gestalt Laws | information-hierarchy | Space groups related things; a rule between two items is an admission that the space did not. |
| P74 | Von Restorff Effect | visual-character | One element per view is allowed to be different; if everything is emphasised, nothing is. |
| P75 | Perfect Card | design-system | Layer a tight shadow for contrast with a soft ambient one for depth, plus a subtle border around 12% opacity. |
| P76 | Depth Layers | design-system | Stack multiple shadows at increasing blur and offset instead of one flat drop shadow. |
| X04 | Modal, toast and popover stacking | design-system | Overlays layer in the order they were opened, and Escape closes the top one only. |
| X06 | Tabs, segments and views | information-hierarchy | A view switch keeps the scroll position and the selection when the user comes back. |
| X07 | Field validation copy | form-ux | An error message names the field, the rule and the fix — not "invalid input". |
| X08 | Selection and focus management | responsive-design | Closing a dialog returns focus to what opened it; removing a row moves focus somewhere sensible. |
| X11 | Reduced data and slow networks | state-completeness | The interface is still usable while images and fonts are missing. |
| X12 | Skip links and landmark structure | responsive-design | The page has one `main`, a heading order that makes sense, and a skip link if the nav is long. |
